title: Instance-adaptive TS augmentation (plain plan)
method: A parametric augmentation network learns per-instance views: a factorization mask h (hard-concrete relaxed Bernoulli per time step from a factorization head), a non-zero transformation mask g (transformation head) and noise η (random time-step masking of the encoder's first hidden layer); both heads share an input layer and a dilated-CNN extractor. The augmenter is trained with a Principle-of-Relevant-Information objective (β·expected L0 of h + mean-embedding discrepancy through the encoder) plus a temporal-consistency loss L_t (λ); the encoder is trained with L_global (InfoNCE) + α·L_local (subsequence contrast). Both are trained from scratch, alternating GAN-style (encoder every step, augmenter every M rounds), each with its own Adam optimizer.

claims.text: The good-view definition preserves task information and adds variance
State of the art on forecasting and classification

questions.text: E1: do the learned representations beat re-run SSL and adaptive-augmentation baselines on univariate and multivariate forecasting and on UCR/UEA classification?
questions.hypothesis: Ours is state of the art on univariate forecasting, multivariate forecasting and classification
questions.predictionIfFalse: The method wins only on long horizons or only on ETT, or gains fall within seed std

questions.text: E2.1: does replacing each framework's hand-crafted augmentation with our augmentation network (loss, encoder and hyperparameters fixed) improve TS2Vec, CoST, TS-TCC and a SimCLR-style InfoNCE baseline, beyond added capacity or training time?
E2.2: does the full objective work with dilated-CNN, LSTM, Transformer and PatchTST-style encoders?
E3.1: on synthetic data with known x* and dataset-dependent optimal augmentations, does our method recover the informative region and approach the oracle?
questions.hypothesis: Our method approaches the oracle, and the best fixed augmentation differs across datasets A and B

questions.text: E3.2: do the predictions of Propositions 1-3 hold (invertible-only views add no information, label preservation, view variance)?
questions.hypothesis: The g-only variant (η off, h ≡ 1) approaches the no-augmentation identity baseline (and may collapse); our views sit at high diversity and high label consistency, while the adversarial generator has high diversity but low consistency

questions.text: E3.3: does one pretrained encoder per dataset, with no task-specific retuning, help forecasting, classification and optionally anomaly detection?
questions.hypothesis: The same augmentations help both tasks

questions.text: E4: which components and design choices of the augmentation network and objectives matter?
E5.1: how does ours with default hyperparameters compare with the best and the median configuration of a grid search over fixed augmentations?
questions.hypothesis: No single fixed augmentation is best on every dataset

questions.text: E5.2: does per-instance adaptivity beat one learned global mask per dataset?
questions.hypothesis: The instance-independent (per-dataset) variant loses, with the largest gap on the E3.1 synthetic data

questions.text: E5.3: do the learned masks recover common augmentations as special cases?
questions.hypothesis: On synthetic data with a known correct augmentation, the learned masks resemble it

questions.text: E5.4: how sensitive is the method to β, λ, α, M, η masking probability, L and τ?
questions.hypothesis: Performance stays flat across reasonable ranges

questions.text: E6: what does the method cost (time, memory, parameters, augmenter overhead vs M) and is training stable?
